'''Irving Martin Isaacs''' (April 14, 1940 – February 17, 2025) was an American [[group theory|group theorist]] and [[representation theory|representation theorist]].  He was a professor of [[mathematics]] at the [[University of Wisconsin&ndash;Madison]].

==Biography==
Isaacs was born in [[the Bronx]], in New York City, on April 14, 1940.<ref name="uwiscmemoriam"/><ref name="americansofscience">{{cite book|title=[[American Men & Women of Science]]|volume=3 (G-I)|edition=22nd|editor1-last=Kalte|editor1-first=Pamela M.|editor2-last=Nemeh|editor2-first=Katherine H.|editor3-last=Schusterbauer|editor3-first=Noah|year=2005|publisher=Thomson Gale}}</ref>  He received a BS from the [[Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn]] in 1960.<ref name="americansofscience"/> While a student there, he was named a Putnam Fellow for his performance in the 1959 [[William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition]].<ref name="NAMS">{{cite journal|title=I. Martin Isaacs (1940–2025)|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|date=December 2025|volume=72|issue=11|pages=1266–1271|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202511/rnoti-p1266.pdf|doi=10.1090/noti3275|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Isaacs went on to [[Harvard University]] for graduate study.  He received a master's degree in 1961,<ref name="americansofscience"/>
and completed his PhD in 1964.  His thesis was advised by [[Richard Brauer]],<ref name=mgp>{{cite web|url=http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=9224|title = I. Martin (Irving) Isaacs|publisher = [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]|accessdate = April 11, 2016}}</ref> and was titled ''Finite <math>p</math>-solvable linear groups''.<ref>{{cite thesis|url=https://id.lib.harvard.edu/alma/990038698240203941/catalog|title=
Finite p-solvable linear groups |last=Isaacs|first=Irving Martin|type=PhD thesis|publisher=Harvard University|year=1964}}</ref>  After a few years at the [[University of Chicago]] as an instructor and visiting assistant professor, Isaacs moved to the [[University of Wisconsin&ndash;Madison]] in 1969.<ref name="americansofscience"/>  He was hired as an associate professor, and promoted to full professor in 1971.<ref name="americansofscience"/>  According to the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]], he supervised 29 doctoral students over his career.<ref name=mgp/>

In 2011, Isaacs retired and became a professor emeritus.<ref name="noticesobit">{{cite journal|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society| title=I. Martin Isaacs (1940–2025)|date=2025|volume=72|issue=11|doi=10.1090/noti3275|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=emeritus-proposal>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.wisc.edu/~passman/emeritus.html|title = Emeritus Professor Proposals|accessdate = May 25, 2014}}</ref><ref name=mathoverflow/>  In retirement, he lived in [[Berkeley, California]] and was an occasional participant on [[MathOverflow]].<ref name=mathoverflow>{{cite web|url=https://mathoverflow.net/users/9694/marty-isaacs|title = User Marty Isaacs|publisher = [[MathOverflow]]|accessdate = May 25, 2014}}</ref>  Near the end of his life, he endowed a prize for "Excellence in Mathematical Writing," first awarded in 2025.<ref name="uwiscmemoriam"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7396|title=Green to Receive Inaugural I. Martin Isaacs Prize |publisher=American Mathematical Society|date=November 26, 2024|access-date=April 7, 2025}}</ref>

==Work==
Isaacs is known as the author of graduate-level textbooks on [[character theory]] and [[group theory]].<ref name="noticesobit"/>  His book ''Character Theory of Finite Groups'' has been described as a classic in the field.<ref name="maarev-ctfg"/>

Isaacs is also known for formulating the Isaacs–Navarro conjecture along with [[Gabriel Navarro Ortega|Gabriel Navarro]], a widely cited generalization of the [[McKay conjecture]].<ref>{{cite journal|title = New refinements of the McKay conjecture for finite groups|last1 = Isaacs|first1 = I. Martin|last2 = Navarro|first2 = Gabriel|journal = [[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume = 156|pages = 333–344|date = 2002|doi=10.2307/3597192|jstor = 3597192|arxiv = math/0411171|s2cid = 16357742}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://groupprops.subwiki.org/wiki/Isaacs-Navarro_conjecture|title = Isaacs-Navarro conjecture|publisher = Groupprops, The Group Properties Wiki|accessdate = May 25, 2014}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Isaacs was seriously injured in an automobile accident in France in 1964, shortly after receiving his PhD.  The accident left him scarred and disabled.<ref name="uwiscmemoriam"/><ref name="noticesobit"/>

He died of kidney failure on February 17, 2025.<ref name="uwiscmemoriam">{{cite web| url=https://math.wisc.edu/memorial-resolution-for-marty-isaacs/ |publisher=University of Wisconsin&ndash;Madison| department=Department of Mathematics|title=Memorial Resolution for Marty Isaacs |last=Passman|first=Don| date=2025|access-date=April 7, 2025}}</ref><ref name="noticesobit"/>

==Awards and honors==
In 2009, a conference was held at the [[Universitat de Valencia]] in [[Spain]] to honor his contributions.<ref name=isaacs-conference>{{cite web|url=http://www.uv.es/isaacs09/|title = Isaacs Conference: Conference on Character Theory of Finite Groups|date = June 3–5, 2009|accessdate = May 25, 2014}}</ref>  Following the conference, a [[festschrift]] was published by the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Character Theory of Finite Groups: Conference in Honor of I. Martin Isaacs |url=https://www.google.si/books/edition/Character_Theory_of_Finite_Groups/KlDUAwAAQBAJ|publisher=American Mathematical Society|series=Contemporary Mathematics|volume=524|editor1-last=Lewis|editor1-first=Mark L.|editor2-last=Navarro|editor2-first=Gabriel|editor3-last=Passman|editor3-first=Donald S.|editor4-last=Wolf|editor4-first=Thomas R.|year=2010|access-date=February 24, 2025}}</ref>

Isaacs was the recipient of a [[Sloan Foundation]] research award in 1971.<ref name="noticesobit"/>  He was inaugurated as a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]] in 2013.<ref name=ams-fellows>{{cite web|url = http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title = List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|publisher = [[American Mathematical Society]]|accessdate = May 25, 2014|archive-date = August 25, 2018|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|url-status = dead}}</ref>

Isaacs was a [[George Pólya|Pólya]] lecturer for the [[Mathematical Association of America]] between 2003 and 2005.<ref name="noticesobit"/>
